kim (Support): Hey team — customer reporting repeated 503s + high latency on POST /v1/generate. They gave a request_id: req_0a1b2c3d4e5f. Can someone search server logs for that ID?

maria (Backend): Sure. Do we have approximate timestamp or the full request body? Need time window to narrow it down.

kim (Support): Customer says ~2026-03-12T16:42:13Z (±2m). They pasted a redacted curl:

kim (Support): ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"open-120b","input":"<redacted>","max_tokens":512}'
```

raja (SRE): On it. Is this a hosted API customer or Dedicated?

kim (Support): Hosted (org_789abcd). No Dedicated.

raja (SRE): Ok. Quick note: prod log retention is 45 days for the centralized index so this should be available. I'll run a request_id search in ES and also check raw s3 logs. Example ES query I run: 

raja (SRE): ```
POST /prod-logs/_search
{
  "query": {
    "term": { "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d4e5f" }
  }
}
```

raja (SRE): Or brute-force on s3: 

raja (SRE): ```bash
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-prod-logs/2026/03/12/prod.log - | grep "req_0a1b2c3d4e5f" -n
```

kim (Support): @ops-collector-bot can you check if a debug bundle exists for that time? :eyes: 

ops-collector-bot: debug bundle created for incident window: debug-1798247000.zip (s3://redwood-debug-bundles/debug-1798247000.zip)

maria (Backend): Found traces in gateway and runner. Gateway shows upstream timeout, runner shows downstream 504 to model-host. 

maria (Backend): Log excerpt: 

maria (Backend): ```
2026-03-12T16:42:13.223Z gateway-1 INFO request_id=req_0a1b2c4... status=502 latency_ms=1203 route=/v1/generate
2026-03-12T16:42:14.101Z runner-3 WARN request_id=req_0a1b2c4... kv_cache=miss model-host=10.4.21.8 timeout=30000ms upstream_status=504
2026-03-12T16:42:15.009Z gateway-1 ERROR request_id=req_0a1b2c4... error="upstream timeout"
```

raja (SRE): I ran the ES query and got 3 hits across gateway/runner/telemetry around 16:42:13-16:44:20. Hosts: gateway-1, runner-3, model-host-ops. I pulled the raw lines and attached an excerpt to this thread.

kim (Support): Can we get a minimal curl reproducer that includes X-Request-Id header so we can match? Asked customer to re-run with this: 

kim (Support): ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c4repro" \n  -d '{"model":"open-120b","input":"test repro","max_tokens":10}'
```

raja (SRE): Since logs are within retention window, I pulled the full raw artifact and uploaded an excerpt to s3: s3://redwood-support-extracts/1798246789/excerpt.log. I also checked for correlated network errors — found TCP RST spikes between runner-3 and model-host around that timestamp.

maria (Backend): Root cause candidate: transient network partition between runner and model-host causing worker timeouts; KV cache miss amplified latency. Opening internal incident INC-2026-487 to track follow-up (routing / peering fixes + retry policy).

kim (Support): I told the customer the likely cause and asked them to retry. Also provided them the debug bundle link and asked for the new repro request_id if they re-run.

ops-collector-bot: uploaded debug bundle: s3://redwood-debug-bundles/debug-1798247000.zip to thread storage.

raja (SRE): Next ops steps: 1) verify network peer health on model-host cluster, 2) add a narrow retry for 504s at runner, 3) validate KV cache hit-rate tuning. I flagged infra.

maria (Backend): I attached exact log pulls in the incident ticket (INC-2026-487) and a suggested patch to make the runner log request_id and shard on start to make future hunts faster.

kim (Support): Customer re-tested and reported success at 16:50Z — no 503s after retry. Closing in support but keeping incident open for infra work. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
